brokeredcredential.title: Credential
brokeredcredential.summary: Owner- and organisation-scoped metadata for a brokered credential — a handle, never the secret.
brokeredcredential.description: Metadata for a secret the credential broker holds on a user's or organisation's behalf. Carries a name, the catalogue provider it targets, the owning user, the scope (personal|organisation), the owning organisation UUID for organisation credentials, and the app ids permitted to use it. MUST NOT contain the secret value: the token is stored in the Nextcloud credential vault (ICredentialsManager), encrypted at rest, keyed by this object's UUID — under the owning user for personal credentials and under a reserved system identity for organisation credentials. No property here is secret-bearing, so the metadata is safe to list, export, audit, and query.

name.description: Human-readable name the owner gives the credential (e.g. "GitHub publisher").
name.title: Name

provider.description: Catalogue provider identifier the credential targets (e.g. "github", "gitlab") — a key in the read-only lib/Settings/credential-providers.json catalogue.
provider.title: Provider

owner.description: The owning user (OR-resolved owner). For a personal credential this is the access-control key: only the owner may read, use, or manage it, and the paired secret is stored under this user in the Nextcloud vault. For an organisation credential this records the provisioning administrator for attribution ONLY — access control is membership of `organisation`, never this field.
owner.title: Owner

scope.description: Access-control scope. `personal` (the default when absent): owner-scoped, the secret lives under the owning user in the Nextcloud vault and only the owner may use or manage it. `organisation`: shared by an organisation, the secret lives under a reserved system identity keyed by this object's UUID and any member of `organisation` may drive a broker call through an allowed app; only an organisation administrator (or a Nextcloud admin) may create, update, or delete it.
scope.title: Scope

organisation.description: The owning OpenRegister organisation UUID. REQUIRED when `scope` is `organisation` (membership of this organisation is the access-control key); MUST be absent/ignored for a personal credential, where it is never an access key.
organisation.title: Organisation

allowedApps.description: App ids the owner has permitted to use this credential via the broker (the per-app allow-list the broker enforces).
allowedApps.title: Allowed Apps

sharedWith.description: Principals this credential is shared with, in addition to its scope. A share grants USE of the credential through the broker — never sight of the secret, which stays in the vault (ADR-004 Rule 1). Only the owner may change this list; a recipient can neither widen it nor re-share onward. A `group` entry is an RBAC permission principal ONLY and is never a tenant discriminator (ADR-002 Rule 1): a principal outside the credential's organisation is denied even when named here. An absent, empty, or malformed list grants nothing.

type.description: Whether `id` names a Nextcloud user or a Nextcloud group.
type.title: Principal type

id.description: The Nextcloud user id or group id.
id.title: User or group

permission.description: What the share grants. `use` lets the recipient drive a brokered call with this credential.
permission.title: Permission granted

sharedWith.title: Shared With

sharedUsers.description: DERIVED from `sharedWith` — do not set directly; the server recomputes it on every write and ignores any client-supplied value. It exists because the RBAC match operator `$contains` compares SCALARS, so it cannot test membership of the object-shaped `sharedWith` entries, and a match clause resolves whole tokens and cannot build `"user:" + $userId` from a prefixed list. Holding bare uids lets a rule say `{"sharedUsers": {"$contains": "$userId"}}`. A stale value here is an access-control bug in either direction, which is why it is never client-writable.
sharedUsers.title: Shared Users

sharedGroups.description: DERIVED from `sharedWith` — see `sharedUsers`. Holds bare group ids so a rule can say `{"sharedGroups": {"$contains": "$user.groups"}}`, which matches when the object lists any one of the caller's groups.
sharedGroups.title: Shared Groups

dataSubjectRequest.title: Data-Subject Request
dataSubjectRequest.summary: A single GDPR / AVG data-subject-rights request tracked as a stateful case.
dataSubjectRequest.description: Jurisdiction-neutral model for a data-subject-rights request tracked as a stateful case: who the subject is, which right is exercised, the request's status in its lifecycle, the EU art-12(3) legal deadline (one month from receipt, extendable once by two months), the assigned handler, case timestamps, retention window, denial workflow, and evidence/redaction sub-collections.

startVerifying.description: Begin verifying the requester's identity / eligibility.

startProgress.description: Begin fulfilling the request (discovery, export, rectify, erase).

fulfil.description: Mark the request fulfilled (the right was honoured).

refuse.description: Refuse the request (a lawful exemption applies).

close.description: Close the request without a fulfil/refuse outcome (e.g. withdrawn).

assign.description: Assign (or reassign) the case to a handler and move it into active verification.

collectEvidence.description: Enter evidence-collection: harvest source data for the case (harvesting itself is delivered by dsar-case-engine).

draftDenial.description: Record a proposed denialGround as a draft denial. Does NOT require a regulatorReference (the gate applies only at finalise).

finaliseDenial.description: Finalise the denial and reach the refused final state. Guarded: refused unless a regulatorReference is present on the case.

redact.description: Record a redaction (field before/after + ground) on the case. The redaction write path is delivered by dsar-case-engine.

bundle.description: Assemble and sign the export bundle and reach the fulfilled final state (bundle generation/signing is delivered by dsar-case-engine).

retain.description: Move a finalised case into its configured retention window (the retention sweep is delivered by dsar-case-engine).

daysRemaining.title: Days Remaining
daysRemaining.description: Whole days between now and the effective deadline (extendedUntil when set, otherwise dueAt). Negative once the deadline has passed. Reuses DataSubjectDeadline art-12 semantics (ADR-011).

isOverdue.title: Is Overdue
isOverdue.description: True when the effective deadline (extendedUntil else dueAt) has passed, i.e. daysRemaining is negative. Reuses DataSubjectDeadline::isOverdue semantics (ADR-011).

escalationTier.title: Escalation Tier
escalationTier.description: Deadline-tracking tier (on-track, reminder, escalation, breached) derived from daysRemaining. The tier boundaries are NOT hard-coded: they resolve from the active dsarPolicyPack's escalationTiers via @ref.pack (index 0 = reminder, 1 = escalation, 2 = breach). The tier activates when the days-past-deadline value (-daysRemaining) reaches a tier's offsetDays; breach when daysRemaining < 0. When no pack resolves (@ref.pack is null) every boundary comparison yields false and the case stays on-track (fail-safe, no false escalation) — the seeded default pack ensures a pack always resolves.

breachedAt.title: Breached At
breachedAt.description: Write-once breach stamp (dsar-escalation-and-dpia): the instant the case's escalationTier first crossed into 'breached'. Declared as a calculation (ADR-031: the temporal sweep job carries no DSAR-specific branch) evaluated AFTER escalationTier in declaration order: while the tier is 'breached' the value coalesces to its existing stamp (write-once) or the evaluation clock on the first crossing; otherwise the existing value (null until a breach) is kept unchanged.

message.nl: De wettelijke termijn voor dit verzoek nadert. Nog {{daysRemaining}} dagen tot de deadline.
message.en: The legal deadline for this request is approaching. {{daysRemaining}} days remaining.

message.nl: Dit verzoek nadert kritiek zijn wettelijke termijn. Nog {{daysRemaining}} dagen.
message.en: This request is critically close to its legal deadline. {{daysRemaining}} days remaining.

message.nl: De wettelijke termijn voor dit verzoek is verstreken.
message.en: The legal deadline for this request has passed.

message.nl: Voor dit verzoek is een Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) gemarkeerd — automatisch patroon (art. 35 AVG) of handmatige markering.
message.en: This request was flagged as requiring a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) — automatic pattern detection (GDPR art. 35) or a manual flag.

x-openregister-seeds.notes: Inwoner vraagt inzage in geregistreerde persoonsgegevens.

x-openregister-seeds.extensionReason: Complex cross-register discovery; single art-12(3) extension applied.

x-openregister-seeds.outcome: Objection refused; compelling legitimate grounds documented; regulator reference recorded.

subjectId.description: Identifier of the data subject (e.g. email or another identifier value indexed in the PII index).
subjectId.title: Subject Identifier

subjectType.description: Optional type hint for the subject identifier (e.g. 'email', 'phone'). Maps to a GdprEntity type when discovering data.
subjectType.title: Subject Type

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction / tenant key selecting which dsarPolicyPack supplies this case's escalation-tier thresholds, denial-ground wording, and retention durations (resolved via the pack cross-object reference). Defaults to 'default', which resolves the jurisdiction-neutral default pack. Full tenant-scoped/override selection semantics are delivered by the successor dsar-integration-seams / dsar-case-ui changes.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

status.description: Lifecycle state of the request (governed by x-openregister-lifecycle).
status.title: Status

receivedAt.description: When the request was received. Anchors the EU art-12 legal deadline.
receivedAt.title: Received At

dueAt.description: EU art-12(3) base legal deadline: receivedAt + 1 month.
dueAt.title: Legal Due Date

extendedUntil.description: Extended legal deadline when a single +2-month extension was granted (art-12(3)). Empty when not extended.
extendedUntil.title: Extended Deadline

extensionReason.description: Justification recorded when the deadline was extended.
extensionReason.title: Extension Reason

outcome.description: Generic outcome summary once the request reaches a final state.
outcome.title: Outcome

notes.description: Free-text handler notes (generic; no jurisdiction policy).
notes.title: Handler Notes

handler.description: Identifier (Nextcloud uid) of the handler the case is assigned to. Used as the recipient for advance-reminder, escalation, and breach notifications.
handler.title: Handler

closedAt.description: When the case was closed (reached a final state). Empty while the case is still open.
closedAt.title: Closed At

dpiaRequired.description: Complexity flag: whether this case requires a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) before it can be fulfilled. Set manually by a handler or automatically by the daily DPIA pattern-detection job (dsar-escalation-and-dpia) when the active policy pack's dpiaDetection threshold is reached; the job never clears a flag (one-way ratchet).
dpiaRequired.title: DPIA Required

breachedAt.description: Write-once stamp of the instant the case's escalationTier first crossed into 'breached'. Populated declaratively by the breachedAt calculation on the tier write that crosses the boundary; empty while the deadline has never been breached. Read by the regulator dossier and breach reporting.
breachedAt.title: Breached At

daysRemaining.description: Engine-materialised value of the daysRemaining calculation (whole days until the effective deadline; negative once passed). Declared as a property so the materialised value persists to a magic-table column — calculation outputs without a backing property are dropped at persist time. Do not edit by hand; the save path and the temporal sweep recompute it.
daysRemaining.title: Days Remaining

isOverdue.description: Engine-materialised value of the isOverdue calculation (true when the effective deadline has passed). Declared as a property so the materialised value persists to a magic-table column and the overdueCaseCount aggregation can filter on it. Do not edit by hand.
isOverdue.title: Is Overdue

escalationTier.description: Engine-materialised value of the escalationTier calculation (on-track, reminder, escalation, breached — boundaries from the active dsarPolicyPack). Declared as a property so the materialised value persists to a magic-table column, the breachedCaseCount aggregation can filter on it, and the calculatedChange notification rules see old/new values. Do not edit by hand; the save path and the temporal sweep recompute it.
escalationTier.title: Escalation Tier

retentionWindow.description: Configured retention window key selecting how long the finalised case dossier is retained before the retention sweep (delivered by dsar-case-engine) may purge it.
retentionWindow.title: Retention Window

retainUntil.description: Computed date until which the finalised case dossier must be retained. Set from receivedAt/closedAt plus the retentionWindow; the retention sweep may purge only after this date.
retainUntil.title: Retain Until

purgedAt.description: When the case dossier was purged by the retention sweep. Empty until the case has been purged.
purgedAt.title: Purged At

denialGround.description: Generic ground key recorded when a case is denied. Jurisdiction-specific statutory wording is Phase-2 policy-pack data and is NOT baked into this schema.
denialGround.title: Denial Ground

regulatorReference.description: Reference recorded for the supervisory authority / regulator when a denial is finalised. Required by the finaliseDenial lifecycle guard before the case may reach the refused final state.
regulatorReference.title: Regulator Reference

evidence.description: Evidence items collected for the case. The item shape is declared here; the harvesting/dedup behaviour is delivered by dsar-case-engine.
evidence.title: Evidence

items.title: Evidence Item
items.description: A single piece of evidence collected for the case, keyed by content hash for downstream deduplication.

sourceId.description: Identifier of the source system or provider the evidence was collected from.
sourceId.title: Source Identifier

contentHash.description: Content hash of the evidence item (e.g. sha256:...), used downstream to deduplicate identical evidence across sources.
contentHash.title: Content Hash

status.description: Per-item collection status (e.g. pending, collected, failed).
status.title: Item Status

redactions.description: Redaction entries recorded on the case. Each entry captures a before/after and the ground, distinct from the erase-time pseudonymise already performed by DataSubjectRequestService. The item shape is declared here; the redaction write path is delivered by dsar-case-engine.
redactions.title: Redactions

items.title: Redaction Entry
items.description: A single redaction applied to a field of the case, with a before/after audit and the ground it was applied under.

field.description: Name of the field that was redacted.
field.title: Redacted Field

before.description: Value of the field before redaction (audit of the original content).
before.title: Value Before

after.description: Value of the field after redaction.
after.title: Value After

ground.description: Generic ground key under which the redaction was applied (e.g. third-party-data).
ground.title: Redaction Ground

dsarPolicyPack.title: AVG/DSAR Policy Pack
dsarPolicyPack.summary: A per-jurisdiction / per-tenant AVG-DSAR policy pack supplying the values the generic data-subject-request workflow resolves from.
dsarPolicyPack.description: Declarative configuration object (ADR-031) holding the jurisdiction-specific AVG/DSAR policy. The generic dataSubjectRequest case resolves its escalation-tier thresholds, denial-ground wording, and retention durations from the ACTIVE pack (selected by the case's jurisdiction, falling back to the jurisdiction-neutral default pack). Every value here is data a steward may edit without a code change. The two seam selectors name which registered provider a jurisdiction binds for identity verification and regulator escalation; an unset or unknown selector is resolved fail-closed to the OR safe-default (refusing) provider by the successor dsar-integration-seams change.

name.description: Human-readable name of this policy pack (e.g. 'Default AVG/DSAR policy pack').
name.title: Pack Name

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction / tenant key that selects this pack for a case (e.g. 'default', 'nl-example'). The neutral fail-closed baseline uses 'default'; a dataSubjectRequest case resolves the pack whose jurisdiction matches the case's jurisdiction field, falling back to the default pack.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction Key

deadlineDurationDays.description: Base statutory response deadline in days measured from receipt (EU art-12(3): one month). Conservative neutral default is 30.
deadlineDurationDays.title: Deadline Duration (days)

extensionDurationDays.description: Additional days granted by the single permitted deadline extension (EU art-12(3): up to two further months). Conservative neutral default is 60.
extensionDurationDays.title: Extension Duration (days)

escalationTiers.description: Ordered deadline-tracking escalation tiers. ORDER IS SIGNIFICANT: index 0 = reminder, index 1 = escalation, index 2 = breach. The dataSubjectRequest escalationTier calculation reads each tier's offsetDays by this position, so a jurisdiction pack MUST keep the three tiers in this order.
escalationTiers.title: Escalation Tiers

items.title: Escalation Tier
items.description: One deadline-tracking tier: a name and the day offset relative to the deadline at which the tier becomes active.

tier.description: Tier name (reminder, escalation, or breach). Used for human display; the case calculation resolves the boundary by array position.
tier.title: Tier Name

offsetDays.description: Day offset relative to the deadline at which this tier activates: negative = before the deadline (e.g. -7 = seven days before), 0 = on the deadline. The case escalationTier calculation activates the tier when daysRemaining <= -offsetDays (breach when daysRemaining < 0).
offsetDays.title: Offset Days

intakeChannels.description: Channels through which a data-subject request may be received in this jurisdiction (e.g. web-form, email, post).
intakeChannels.title: Intake Channels

roleMapping.description: Maps the abstract case roles to the jurisdiction's role identifiers (ADR-023). Placeholders (<role-id>) are used in seed data; a leaf app binds real Nextcloud group/role ids.
roleMapping.title: Role Mapping

dpo.description: Role identifier for the Data Protection Officer (used in jurisdictions with a DPO).
dpo.title: DPO Role

fg.description: Role identifier for the Functionaris Gegevensbescherming (the NL-context equivalent of a DPO).
fg.title: FG Role

handler.description: Role identifier for the case handler who processes the request day to day.
handler.title: Handler Role

templates.description: References to the letter / notification templates this jurisdiction uses (template: references resolved by a document leaf per ADR-022; not inline content).
templates.title: Template References

acknowledgement.description: Template reference for the request-acknowledgement letter sent on intake.
acknowledgement.title: Acknowledgement Template

denial.description: Template reference for the denial letter sent when a request is refused.
denial.title: Denial Template

extension.description: Template reference for the deadline-extension notice sent when the deadline is extended.
extension.title: Extension Template

denialGrounds.description: Maps each generic Phase-1 denial-ground key to this jurisdiction's human wording and statutory citation. The generic keys live on the dataSubjectRequest schema; the jurisdiction label + citation live here.
denialGrounds.title: Denial Grounds

items.title: Denial Ground
items.description: One denial-ground mapping: a generic key plus the jurisdiction label and statutory citation shown to handlers and data subjects.

key.description: Generic denial-ground key matching a value of the dataSubjectRequest denialGround enum (e.g. manifestly-unfounded, third-party-rights).
key.title: Ground Key

label.description: Jurisdiction-specific human-readable label for this denial ground.
label.title: Ground Label

citation.description: Statutory citation supporting this denial ground (illustrative in the shipped example packs; authoritative wording is supplied by the leaf consumer).
citation.title: Statutory Citation

retentionWindows.description: Named retention windows this jurisdiction offers. Each maps a window key (selected by the case's retentionWindow field) to a duration; the consuming retention engine computes retainUntil from the finalisation date plus this duration.
retentionWindows.title: Retention Windows

items.title: Retention Window
items.description: One named retention window: a key selectable on a case and the duration the finalised dossier is retained.

key.description: Retention-window key matching the dataSubjectRequest retentionWindow selector (e.g. standard, extended).
key.title: Window Key

durationMonths.description: Number of months a finalised case dossier is retained under this window before the retention sweep may purge it.
durationMonths.title: Duration (months)

privacyOfficerGroup.description: Nextcloud group id of this jurisdiction's privacy officer (DPO/FG) team. Resolved by the declared deadlineBreach and dpiaFlagged notification recipients (PrivacyOfficerRecipientResolver) so breach and DPIA visibility reach the officer without hard-coding a group in the case schema. Unset, placeholder (<...>), or unknown groups resolve to zero officer recipients (fail-safe — the handler recipient still receives the notification).
privacyOfficerGroup.title: Privacy-Officer Group

dpiaDetection.description: GDPR art-35 DPIA pattern-detection configuration read by the daily detection job (dsar-escalation-and-dpia). Absent block = detection disabled for this jurisdiction (fail-safe: no false DPIA flags). The seeded default pack carries the pipelinq-parity defaults (threshold 10, window 30 days, group by type + scope).
dpiaDetection.title: DPIA Detection

threshold.description: Minimum number of similar cases inside the rolling window that triggers the DPIA flag on the whole group.
threshold.title: Threshold

windowDays.description: Rolling-window length in days over which similar cases are counted (receivedAt based).
windowDays.title: Window (days)

groupBy.description: Case fields whose normalised values (trim/lowercase/collapse-whitespace) define 'similar' — cases sharing every listed value form one group.
groupBy.title: Group By

items.title: Grouping Field
items.description: A dataSubjectRequest field name used as a grouping characteristic.

identityVerifyProvider.description: Selector naming the registered identity-verify seam provider this jurisdiction binds. Unset or unknown resolves fail-closed to the OR safe-default (refusing) provider id (never fail-open); the default pack sets this to or.default.identity-verify.null. Provider interface/registry/resolution are delivered by the successor dsar-integration-seams change.
identityVerifyProvider.title: Identity-Verify Provider

regulatorEscalateProvider.description: Selector naming the registered regulator-escalate seam provider this jurisdiction binds. Unset or unknown resolves fail-closed to the OR safe-default (refusing) provider id (never fail-open); the default pack sets this to or.default.regulator-escalate.null. Provider interface/registry/resolution are delivered by the successor dsar-integration-seams change.
regulatorEscalateProvider.title: Regulator-Escalate Provider

edepotTransfer.title: e-Depot Transfer List
edepotTransfer.summary: A durable e-Depot transfer list tracked through its review-approve-execute status machine.
edepotTransfer.description: The durable record of an e-Depot transfer: which objects are pending/approved/completed, archivist approvals + exclusions, the append-only history of delivery attempts (long-horizon retry), the final transfer result, and the SIP package format/identity. Persisted through ObjectService so status transitions ride OR's audited write path (making TransferController's former placeholder responses real).

objectReferences.description: Objects included in this transfer, each as {uuid, schema, register}.
objectReferences.title: Object References

items.title: Object Reference
items.description: A reference to one object included in the transfer.

uuid.title: Object UUID
uuid.description: UUID of the object included in the transfer.

schema.title: Schema Id
schema.description: Identifier of the schema the referenced object belongs to.

register.title: Register Id
register.description: Identifier of the register the referenced object belongs to.

exclusions.description: Objects excluded from the transfer during review, each with a reason and timestamp.
exclusions.title: Exclusions

uuid.title: Object UUID
uuid.description: UUID of the object excluded from the transfer.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Human-readable reason the object was excluded during review.

excludedAt.title: Excluded At
excludedAt.description: Timestamp at which the object was excluded from the transfer.

approvalMetadata.description: Archivist approval / rejection metadata (who, when, rejection reason).
approvalMetadata.title: Approval Metadata

attempts.description: Append-only history of delivery attempts (long-horizon retry): attempt number, timestamp, transport, per-package outcome, and error. Never rewritten — the WebhookLog attempt semantics, stored on this durable aggregate.
attempts.title: Delivery Attempts

items.title: Delivery Attempt
items.description: One transport attempt for the transfer.

attempt.title: Attempt Number
attempt.description: Sequential number of this delivery attempt.

timestamp.title: Attempted At
timestamp.description: Timestamp at which this delivery attempt was made.

transport.title: Transport
transport.description: Transport channel used for this delivery attempt.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: Per-package outcome of this delivery attempt.

error.title: Error
error.description: Error detail captured when the delivery attempt failed.

transferResult.description: The final transfer result (completion timestamp + per-object outcomes).
transferResult.title: Transfer Result

packageFormat.description: SIP serialization format used for this transfer.
packageFormat.title: Package Format

createdAt.description: When the transfer list was created.
createdAt.title: Created At

edepotTransferProof.title: e-Depot Proof of Transfer
edepotTransferProof.summary: An immutable proof-of-transfer record for one object confirmed ingested by an e-Depot.
edepotTransferProof.description: The durable, write-once ingest-confirmation artefact an archivist or auditor can produce years later (Archiefwet accountability). Created per confirmed object when the transfer completes; captures the e-Depot ingest reference/archivId + raw transport receipt, the SIP package identity (id, format, manifest SHA-256), and the per-file checksums as sent. Immutable (schema-level + service-level refusal); lives in this system register so destruction of the source object after handover never cascades to it. procest's retired archiefBewijs records migrate 1:1 onto this schema.

objectUuid.description: UUID of the transferred (confirmed) object this proof attests.
objectUuid.title: Object UUID

transferUuid.description: UUID of the edepotTransfer list this proof belongs to.
transferUuid.title: Transfer UUID

eDepotReference.description: The e-Depot ingest reference / archivId returned on confirmation.
eDepotReference.title: e-Depot Reference

transportReceipt.description: Raw transport receipt / confirmation payload as returned by the e-Depot (opaque).
transportReceipt.title: Transport Receipt

transportName.description: Name of the transport used (sftp, rest_api, openconnector).
transportName.title: Transport

packageId.description: Identity of the SIP package the object was delivered in.
packageId.title: Package Id

packageFormat.description: SIP serialization format of the delivered package.
packageFormat.title: Package Format

packageManifestSha256.description: SHA-256 over the package payload manifest (the manifest-sha256.txt content for bagit, the sip-manifest.json content for zip).
packageManifestSha256.title: Package Manifest SHA-256

fileChecksums.description: Per-file checksums as sent, each {name, sha256}.
fileChecksums.title: File Checksums

items.title: File Checksum
items.description: One payload file's name and SHA-256.

name.title: File Name
name.description: Name of the payload file included in the transfer.

sha256.title: SHA-256
sha256.description: SHA-256 checksum of the payload file as sent.

confirmedAt.description: When the e-Depot confirmed ingest of this object.
confirmedAt.title: Confirmed At

flow.title: Flow
flow.summary: A flow definition the OpenRegister flow engine walks.
flow.description: A flow is a graph of nodes and edges. Each edge carries the step to run (its `type` names a registered flow node such as openregister.set-fields, openregister.route or openregister.sub-flow, and `config` its options); the engine walks the graph, threading an item list from step to step. `trigger` (with optional `triggerRegister` / `triggerSchema`) wires the flow to an event so it runs automatically; `enabled` must be true for a trigger to fire it.

enabled.description: Whether the flow is active. A trigger only fires an enabled flow.
enabled.title: Enabled

trigger.description: The event that starts the flow (a catalog trigger id such as object.created, file.created, tag.assigned; manual for a flow run only on request; or schedule to run it on a cron).
trigger.title: Trigger

cron.description: For a schedule trigger: the cron expression that decides when the flow runs (e.g. "0 9 * * 1" = 09:00 every Monday). Ignored for other triggers.
cron.title: Cron schedule

executionMode.description: When to run the flow relative to what triggered it. async (the default) queues the run and a background worker picks it up within a minute. sync runs the flow inside the triggering action, so its effects are complete before that action returns — choose it only when a caller genuinely depends on that, because the flow then runs on someone's critical path and a slow flow means a slow save. A sync flow that hits a wait is left for the worker rather than blocking.
executionMode.title: Execution mode

sharedWith.description: Principals this flow is shared with. `read` lets the recipient see the flow; `run` lets them trigger it and implies `read`. A share NEVER grants edit, so a recipient can change neither the flow's definition, nor this list, nor `credentialIdentity` — a share cannot be used to widen itself or to redirect the flow at other credentials. Only the owner manages it. A share does not carry the flow's run history: a recipient sees only the runs they triggered themselves, because a run log records the subject data the flow touched. A `group` entry is an RBAC permission principal only, never a tenant discriminator (ADR-002 Rule 1).

type.description: Whether `id` names a Nextcloud user or a Nextcloud group.
type.title: Principal type

id.description: The Nextcloud user id or group id.
id.title: User or group

permission.description: What the share grants. `run` implies `read`. Enforced in TWO places by necessity: RBAC grants visibility of the object, and the trigger endpoint enforces the verb — `run` is not an object RBAC action (those are create/read/update/delete), so a read-only recipient who can see the flow must still be refused at the trigger.
permission.title: Permission granted

sharedWith.title: Shared With

sharedUsers.description: DERIVED from `sharedWith` — do not set directly; the server recomputes it on every write and ignores any client-supplied value. The RBAC match operator `$contains` compares SCALARS, so it cannot test membership of the object-shaped `sharedWith` entries, and a match clause resolves whole tokens and cannot build `"user:" + $userId` from a prefixed list. Holding bare uids lets a rule say `{"sharedUsers": {"$contains": "$userId"}}`. A stale value here is an access-control bug in either direction, which is why it is never client-writable.
sharedUsers.title: Shared Users

sharedGroups.description: DERIVED from `sharedWith` — see `sharedUsers`. Holds bare group ids so a rule can say `{"sharedGroups": {"$contains": "$user.groups"}}`, which matches when the object lists any one of the caller's groups.
sharedGroups.title: Shared Groups

credentialIdentity.description: Whose credentials a run of this flow resolves as. `runner` (the default, and what happens today when absent): credentials resolve as the user who triggered the run, so a share recipient runs it with their OWN credentials and the run fails closed if they hold none. `owner`: the flow LENDS the owner's credential — it resolves as the flow owner whatever who triggered it. `owner` is a deliberate delegation of the owner's authority, so only the owner may set it and a share recipient can never flip it. It grants USE of the credential, never sight: resolution still goes through the broker, which returns no plaintext secret on its routed path. Every run records the identity it resolved as, separately from the identity that triggered it, so a lent-credential call stays attributable.
credentialIdentity.title: Credential identity

triggerRegister.description: Restrict an object-event trigger to one register (empty = any).
triggerRegister.title: Trigger register

triggerSchema.description: Restrict an object-event trigger to one schema (empty = any).
triggerSchema.title: Trigger schema

nodes.description: The flow's nodes; each carries an id.
nodes.title: Nodes

edges.description: The flow's edges; each carries from/to plus the step type and config to run.
edges.title: Edges

mergeOperation.title: Merge Operation
mergeOperation.summary: An audit row for one executed (or reversed) merge.
mergeOperation.description: Written exactly once by MergeService::executeMerge() and updated by MergeService::reverseMerge(). Captures the survivor, the merged-away objects, the reason, and a preMergeSnapshot sufficient to restore both objects within the reversal window.

mergedFromUuids.description: UUIDs of the losing objects merged away into the survivor.
mergedFromUuids.title: Merged From

preMergeSnapshot.description: Both objects' golden record, provenance, status and linked source-record ownership, sufficient to restore them on reversal.
preMergeSnapshot.title: Pre-Merge Snapshot

reversible.description: Whether this operation can still be reversed (false once reversed or the window has elapsed).
reversible.title: Reversible

reversedAt.description: Timestamp the merge was reversed, when applicable.
reversedAt.title: Reversed At

reversedBy.description: Acting user uid that reversed the merge, when applicable.
reversedBy.title: Reversed By

trustConfiguration.title: Trust Configuration
trustConfiguration.summary: A trust-tier rule for one (entityType, attribute, sourceSystem) tuple.
trustConfiguration.description: One row declares which trust tier a source system's value earns for a given entity type + attribute, optionally with a freshness-decay window and an effectiveFrom date for versioning. TrustTierResolver looks up the most recent row whose effectiveFrom is on/before the as-of date; when no row matches, the caller falls back to the annotation's defaultTier.

entityType.description: The master-record entity type this rule applies to (e.g. 'organisation'). Never hardcoded by the engine.
entityType.title: Entity Type

attribute.description: The attribute name this rule applies to (e.g. 'legalName', 'email').
attribute.title: Attribute

sourceSystem.description: Slug of the source system this rule applies to (e.g. 'municipal-registry').
sourceSystem.title: Source System

trustTier.description: The trust tier this source earns for this attribute.
trustTier.title: Trust Tier

freshnessDecayDays.description: Days after which a source's value for this attribute steps one tier down (freshness decay). Omit/null for no decay.
freshnessDecayDays.title: Freshness Decay (days)

effectiveFrom.description: Date this rule takes effect. Among matching rows, the most recent effectiveFrom on/before the as-of date wins (time-versioned).
effectiveFrom.title: Effective From

concept.title: Concept
concept.summary: A SKOS concept (a single controlled-vocabulary term)
concept.description: A single term within a concept scheme (SKOS Concept), e.g. one Woo informatiecategorie. Identified durably by its source URI; the importer keys upserts on this URI and, on re-import, marks concepts missing from the source as deprecated rather than deleting them (leaf apps hold long-lived references).

uri.description: The canonical, durable URI that identifies this concept (e.g. a TOOI kern-thesaurus concept URI such as https://identifier.overheid.nl/tooi/def/thes/kern/c_139c6280). Unique within the register: the importer's URI-keyed upsert never creates a second concept object for the same uri.
uri.title: Concept URI

prefLabel.description: Preferred human-readable label for this concept, keyed by BCP-47 language tag. Dutch ("nl") is required; additional language tags (e.g. "en") are optional. Used for display and for the resolution API's cross-language label search.

nl.description: The Dutch (nl) preferred label of this concept.
nl.title: Dutch Preferred Label

en.description: The English (en) preferred label of this concept, when the source publishes one.
en.title: English Preferred Label

additionalProperties.description: A preferred label in an additional BCP-47 language tag not listed above.
additionalProperties.title: Additional-Language Preferred Label

prefLabel.title: Preferred Label

altLabel.description: Alternative human-readable labels (synonyms) for this concept, keyed by BCP-47 language tag, matching the shape of prefLabel. Optional; used by the resolution API's label search to also match on known synonyms.

nl.description: A Dutch (nl) alternative label (synonym) for this concept.
nl.title: Dutch Alternative Label

en.description: An English (en) alternative label (synonym) for this concept.
en.title: English Alternative Label

additionalProperties.description: An alternative label in an additional BCP-47 language tag not listed above.
additionalProperties.title: Additional-Language Alternative Label

altLabel.title: Alternative Label

definition.description: A statement or formal explanation of the meaning of this concept, as published by the source.
definition.title: Definition

notation.description: A compact, source-defined code identifying this concept within its scheme (e.g. a TOOI "c_..." identifier), distinct from the durable uri. Used by the resolution API's (scheme, notation) lookup.
notation.title: Notation

deprecated.description: Whether this concept has been withdrawn from the upstream source. Set by the importer when a re-imported source no longer contains this concept's uri; the concept is never deleted so existing leaf references keep resolving.
deprecated.title: Deprecated

inScheme.description: Reference to the conceptScheme this concept belongs to.
inScheme.title: In Scheme

broader.description: References to broader (more general) sibling concepts in the hierarchy. Maintained by the importer in both directions: when concept A is broader of B, B's broader lists A and A's narrower lists B.
broader.title: Broader Concepts

narrower.description: References to narrower (more specific) sibling concepts in the hierarchy. Maintained by the importer in both directions: when concept A is broader of B, B's broader lists A and A's narrower lists B.
narrower.title: Narrower Concepts

related.description: References to associatively related sibling concepts (SKOS skos:related) that are neither broader nor narrower.
related.title: Related Concepts

conceptScheme.title: Concept Scheme
conceptScheme.summary: A SKOS concept scheme (controlled vocabulary / begrippenkader)
conceptScheme.description: A named, published controlled vocabulary (SKOS ConceptScheme) that groups a set of concepts, e.g. the Woo informatiecategorieën or a GEMMA referentiecomponenten-lijst. Identified durably by its source URI; imported/refreshed via the VocabularyImportService.

uri.description: The canonical, durable URI that identifies this concept scheme (e.g. a TOOI kern-thesaurus base URI or a GEMMA scheme URI). Unique within the register: the importer's URI-keyed upsert never creates a second conceptScheme object for the same uri.
uri.title: Scheme URI

title.description: Human-readable name of the concept scheme, as published by the source (e.g. "Woo-informatiecategorieën").
title.title: Title

description.description: Optional longer description of the concept scheme's purpose and scope, as published by the source.
description.title: Description

publisher.description: The organisation responsible for publishing and maintaining this concept scheme (e.g. "KOOP" or a TOOI organisatie URI).
publisher.title: Publisher

version.description: Version identifier of the concept scheme as published upstream, used by the importer to detect an updated source release.
version.title: Version

source.description: URI or identifier of the upstream source this scheme was imported from (e.g. a TOOI waardelijst identifier or a SKOS/JSON-LD export URL).
source.title: Source
